entryPointUI.title: Entrypoints
entryPointUI.subtitle: The ports Traefik listens on, and what happens to traffic arriving on each one.
entryPointUI.search: Search entrypoints, ports or redirect targets…
entryPointUI.emptyHelp: Create an entrypoint so routers have a port to receive traffic on.
entryPointUI.adjustFilters: Change the search or clear filters.
entryPointUI.name: Name
entryPointUI.nameLocked: The name cannot be changed. Routers refer to the entrypoint by it.

kind.label: Type
kind.help: What the entrypoint is for. It decides the protocol and which settings apply.
kind.httpHelp: Web traffic. TLS is decided by each router. Usually port 80.
kind.httpsHelp: Web traffic with TLS turned on for every router. Usually port 443.
kind.tcpHelp: A plain port for a database, MQTT, SSH or another TCP protocol. No HTTP settings.
kind.udpHelp: A UDP port, for example DNS on 53. Only UDP routers can use it.

entryPointUI.nameHelp: Routers refer to the entrypoint by this name. Start with a lowercase letter; use letters, digits, hyphens or underscores (1–63 characters). It cannot be changed later.
entryPointUI.protocolTcpHelp: Web and TCP entrypoints listen on TCP.
entryPointUI.protocolUdpHelp: A UDP entrypoint listens on UDP.
entryPointUI.portHelp: 1–65535. The port must also be published on the Traefik container.
entryPointUI.hostHelp: Optional. Leave empty to listen on every network interface.
entryPointUI.asDefault: Use for routers that do not name an entrypoint
entryPointUI.asDefaultHelp: Without any default, such routers listen on every TCP entrypoint. Mark the entrypoints they should use.
entryPointUI.reusePort: Share the port with other listeners (SO_REUSEPORT)
entryPointUI.reusePortHelp: For several Traefik processes on one host. Linux, BSD and macOS only. Leave off unless you need it.
entryPointUI.udpTimeoutHelp: How long an idle UDP session is kept before its resources are released.
entryPointUI.trustedIPsHelp: IP addresses or CIDR ranges of your proxies and load balancers. Press Enter after each one.

http.redirect: Redirect all requests to another entrypoint
http.redirectHelp: Traefik answers with a redirect before any router is consulted.
http.redirectPortHelp: Use this when the public port differs from an entrypoint's port, for example behind port forwarding.
http.allowAcmeBypassHelp: Requests for /.well-known/acme-challenge/ are not redirected, so your own routers can answer certificate challenges.
http.redirectPriorityHelp: The redirect is a router. A router of yours with a higher priority on this entrypoint is served instead of being redirected.
http.tlsSectionHelp: Defaults for the routers on this entrypoint. A router with its own TLS settings replaces them entirely.
http.tlsPerRouter: TLS is decided by each router on this entrypoint. To turn it on for every router, change the type to Secure web (HTTPS).
http.tlsWithRedirect: This entrypoint redirects everything, so these TLS defaults only matter for routers with a higher priority than the redirect.
http.certResolverHelp: Requests certificates for routers that do not choose a resolver themselves.
http.noResolverNote: Without a resolver Traefik serves a matching uploaded certificate, or its self-signed default.
http.tlsDomainsHelp: Optional. Request these certificates (for example a wildcard) instead of one per router host name.
http.tlsOptionsHelp: Name of a TLS options set (minimum version, ciphers). Add @file for one from a dynamic file. Empty uses “default”.
http.http3Help: Traefik also listens on UDP port {port}. Publish that port for UDP as well.
http.http3NeedsTls: HTTP/3 only serves routers that have TLS. Make sure the routers here set it, or use the Secure web (HTTPS) type.
http.http3PortHelp: The UDP port clients are told to use. Change it only when the public port differs.
http.middlewaresHelp: Applied in order before each router's own middlewares. A missing middleware breaks every router on this entrypoint.
http.middlewareOther: Use a middleware from another provider
http.middlewareOtherHelp: Name and provider, for example auth@docker.

forwarded.sectionHelp: Whose X-Forwarded-For and similar headers are believed. Needed to see real visitor addresses behind a proxy or CDN.
forwarded.noneHelp: Traefik replaces these headers with what it sees itself. Right when clients connect directly.
forwarded.listHelp: Only the proxies and load balancers you list. Right behind a CDN or load balancer.
forwarded.allHelp: Any client can claim any address. For tests only.
forwarded.allWarning: Every client can fake its address, which defeats IP allow lists, rate limits and CrowdSec decisions. Use this for tests only.
forwarded.connectionHelp: Headers named in the Connection header that should reach your middlewares before being removed.
forwarded.notAppend: Do not add the client address to X-Forwarded-For
forwarded.notAppendHelp: Keep the header exactly as received.

proxy.sectionHelp: For a TCP load balancer that passes the visitor's address in a PROXY protocol header (v1 or v2).
proxy.noneHelp: Connections do not start with a PROXY header.
proxy.listHelp: Only the addresses you list may send the header.
proxy.allHelp: Any client may send the header. For tests only.
proxy.enabledWarning: Turn PROXY protocol on at the load balancer too. If only one side has it, connections fail.
proxy.allWarning: Any client can fake its address with a PROXY header. Use this for tests only, and turn it on at the load balancer too.

advanced.intro: Everything here is optional: an empty field keeps Traefik's default. Durations are written like 30s or 2m; 0 disables a limit.
advanced.readTimeoutHelp: Maximum time to read a whole request, body included.
advanced.writeTimeoutHelp: Maximum time to write a response.
advanced.idleTimeoutHelp: How long an idle keep-alive connection stays open.
advanced.keepAliveMaxTimeHelp: Close a keep-alive connection after this long.
advanced.keepAliveMaxRequestsHelp: Close a keep-alive connection after this many requests.
advanced.graceTimeoutHelp: How long running requests get to complete.
advanced.requestAcceptGraceTimeoutHelp: Delay before shutdown begins, so a load balancer can notice.
advanced.maxHeaderBytesHelp: Requests with larger headers are refused.
advanced.deniedCharacters: Refuse encoded characters in the path
advanced.deniedCharactersHelp: Traefik accepts all of these by default. Tick the ones to refuse.
advanced.aliasHeadersHelp: Header names that collide with another header once normalised, such as underscores for dashes.
advanced.encodeQuerySemicolons: Encode semicolons in the query string
advanced.encodeQuerySemicolonsHelp: Stops services from reading a semicolon as a parameter separator.
advanced.sanitizePathHelp: Removes /./, /../ and repeated slashes before routing.
advanced.sanitizePathWarning: With this off, paths such as /admin/../secret reach routers and services unchanged. Only turn it off for a service that needs raw paths.
advanced.maxConcurrentStreamsHelp: Streams a client may open on one connection.
advanced.observabilityHelp: Defaults for routers on this entrypoint. A router can override them.
advanced.traceVerbosityHelp: Detailed adds a span for every middleware.
